full_judgment:
2. Petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 80 of 1988 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Dumuria, Khulna for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 28th February 1987 of the learned Munsif, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Suit No. 537 of 1981. Its case in short is that the respondent Nos. 1- 3 instituted Title Suit No. 537 of 1981 in the First Court of Munsif, Khulna against the Assistant Custodian, Vested and Non-resident Property and others. The said suit was decreed on 28 February, 1987 in favour of the .respondents which was obtained collusively, and the petitioner on coming to know about the collusive decree removed the panel lawyer of the Vested Property authority, and thereupon, obtained the necessary papers and ascertained that the decree was collusively obtained and accordingly instituted the suit seeking the above relief. 

 3. The respondent Nos. 1-3 entered appearance in the suit and filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and prayed for rejection of the plaint calming that the plaintiffs suit is hit by the principles of res-judicata, inasmuch as, in their earlier suit being Title Suit No. 537 of 1981 they made 7 defendants, of them, the defendant No. 6 was the Assistant Custodian, Vested and Non-resident Property, Khulna, while the defendant No. 7 was the government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna. The said defendants filed written statements separately but the defendant No. 6 ultimately did not contest the suit. The Deputy Commissioner Khulna though did not adduce any evidence but cross-examined the plaintiffs witnesses. In the premises, the suit having been decreed on contest the subsequent suit at the instance of the petitioner is not legally maintainable. 

 "I. For that the ex-parte decree in Title Suit No. 537 of 1981 in the court of learned Munsif, 1st Court, Khulna having being obtained collusively the same being liable to be canceled, the High Court Division erred in law in setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 155 of 1990 allowing the appeal." 

 "IV. For that the suit filed by the present petitioners not having barred as 'resjudicata' the application under Order 7, Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure not being maintainable, the High Court Division erred in law in making the rule absolute." "V. For that the High Court Division erred in law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the learned appellate Court below erroneously holding that the issues of both the title Suit No. 537 of 1981 and Title Suit No. 80 of 1988 are directly and substantially the same as contemplated in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and as such the trial court below came to correct finding that the plaint in Title Suit No. 80 of 1988 is hit by the provision of Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908."
